## Comparability caveat

Before the ranking: **Alaska's FY2024 figures are not fully comparable to the other four carriers on a like-for-like basis.** Alaska completed its acquisition of Hawaiian Holdings on September 18, 2024, and Hawaiian's results are consolidated only from that date forward [DOC-2]. That partial-period inclusion added $869 million of revenue and a $113 million net loss to Alaska's FY2024 consolidated results [DOC-2], so Alaska's full-year margins blend roughly 8.5 months of standalone Alaska with ~3.5 months of a dilutive acquisition. All five companies do at least share the same calendar fiscal year (Jan 1 – Dec 31) [DOC-1], so there is no fiscal-year mismatch.

## Operating margin, FY2024 (operating income ÷ revenue)

| Rank | Airline | Operating income | Revenue | Margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Delta | $5,995M | $61,643M | 9.7% [DOC-1] |
| 2 | United | $5,096M | $57,063M | 8.9% [DOC-1] |
| 3 | Alaska | $570M | $11,735M | 4.86% [DOC-1] |
| 4 | American | $2,614M | $54,211M | 4.82% [DOC-1] |
| 5 | Southwest | $321M | $27,483M | 1.2% [DOC-1] |

Note that Alaska vs. American is effectively a tie (a ~4 basis-point gap); given the Hawaiian partial-period distortion [DOC-2], that ordering should not be treated as meaningful.

## Net margin, FY2024 (net income ÷ revenue)

| Rank | Airline | Net income | Revenue | Margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Delta | $3,457M | $61,643M | 5.6% [DOC-1] |
| 2 | United | $3,149M | $57,063M | 5.5% [DOC-1] |
| 3 | Alaska | $395M | $11,735M | 3.4% [DOC-1] |
| 4 | Southwest | $465M | $27,483M | 1.7% [DOC-1] |
| 5 | American | $846M | $54,211M | 1.6% [DOC-1] |

Backing out Hawaiian's contribution ($869M revenue, $113M net loss [DOC-2]), Alaska's standalone net margin would be roughly 4.7% ($508M / $10,866M) — still third, behind United.

## Answer

Delta ranks first on both measures, with United second and Southwest/American at the bottom (their relative order flips between the two rankings because American's operating income of $2,614M converts to only $846M of net income [DOC-1], while Southwest's $465M net income exceeds its $321M operating income [DOC-1]).

ANSWER: Yes — Delta is top-ranked on both. Operating margin: Delta 9.7% > United 8.9% > Alaska 4.86% > American 4.82% > Southwest 1.2%. Net margin: Delta 5.6% > United 5.5% > Alaska 3.4% > Southwest 1.7% > American 1.6%. (Alaska's figures include Hawaiian only from Sept 18, 2024, so they are not strictly comparable, and the Alaska/American operating-margin gap is within rounding noise.)
